div.head: III Eg 7
div.ab: ⁊ se ðe tihtbysig sý ⁊ folce ungetriwe ⁊ þas gemot forbuge, þonne sceawie man of ðam gemote þa þe him toridan, ⁊ finde him þonne gyt borh, gyf he mæge.
⁊ se þe tihtbysig sy ⁊ folce ungetrywe ⁊ þas gemót forbuge ðriwa, þonne sceapige mon of þam gemote ða ðe him tórídon, ⁊ finde him þonne gyt borh, gyf he mæge.
⁊ se ðe tyhtbysig sy ⁊ folce ungetrywe ⁊ þas gemot forbuge þrywa, þonne scawie man of þam gemote þa ðe him tóridan, ⁊ finde þonne gyt borh, gif he mæge.
Et qui fuerit accusationibus infamatus et populo incredibilis et hec placita declinauerit, uideatur de (ipso) placito qui mittantur ad eum, et inueniat etiam tunc sibi fideiussores, si possit.
[Be tyhtbysigum.] [Ld] ⁊ se þe tihtbisig sy ⁊ folce ungetrywe ⁊ þas gemot forbuge þrywa, þonne scifte man of þam gemote ða ðe him toridan, ⁊ finde þonne git borh, gif he mæge.
And se ðe tyhtbysig sy and folce ungetriwe and þas gemot forbuge þriwa, þonne sceawie man of ðam gemote þa þe him to ridan. And finde him þonne gyt borh, gyf he mæge.

And if anyone who has a bad reputation and is unworthy of public confidence fails to attend the court-meetings three times, men shall be chosen from the meeting who shall ride to him, and he may then still find a surety, if he can.

And if anyone who is disreputable or deemed untrustworthy by the community fails to attend public meetings three times, then let three men of that meeting be chosen to ride to him. And he may still find a surety, if he can.

And he who is frequently accused and is unworthy of the people’s trust, and who fails to attend these meetings—then men are to be chosen from the meeting to ride to him; and he may still provide a surety, if he can.

(Von oft Bescholtenen. Ld) Und wer oft bescholten ist und der Allgemeinheit Vertrauens unwürdig [gilt] und diese Gerichtsversammlungen dreimal (fehlt G Qu.) vermeidet: dann möge man aus der Gerichtsversammlung die [Männer] aussuchen (abordnen D), welche zu ihm ziehen sollen, und er mag sich [auch] dann noch Bürgschaft finden, wenn er kann.

(Of those often accused. Ld) And whoever is often accused and [held] untrustworthy by the people and avoids these court-meetings three times (lacking in G, Qu.): then let [men] be chosen (appointed, D) from the court-meeting to ride to him, and let him [even] then still find himself a surety, if he can.
div.note: II As 20; II As 20.1; II As 20.4
‘þriwa’ should be supplied in G from II As 20, A, D, G2 and II Cn 25. A's ‘sceapige’ also in the copy in B. Liebermann compares II As 20, 20.1, 20.4.
The Wulfstan MSS and Quit’s laws add “three times”. It is not in Quadripartitus and is probably a Wulfstan addition.
